name: SkeletonBox
statusNote: Alpha in Primer React. It is the primitive under SkeletonText and SkeletonAvatar, which share its fill and shimmer.
summary: A muted rounded rectangle that stands in for content of known shape while it loads, shimmering unless the user prefers reduced motion. Use SkeletonText for text lines and SkeletonAvatar for avatars; use Spinner when the shape is unknown.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Any CSS width; unset fills the container (block).

inputs.name: delay
inputs.description: Render nothing until the delay passes: short 300ms, long 1000ms, or a number of ms.

layout.text: The box is a block: full container width unless width is given, 16px (1rem) tall unless height is given, with --borderRadius-small corners.

states.text: With no reduced-motion preference the fill shimmers: its opacity is masked by a 75deg gradient (opaque to 30%, 65% opaque from 80%) twice the box's width, which slides across it once per --base-duration-1000 (1000ms), forever, with CSS's default ease curve. With reduced motion the box is static.

behaviour.text: The shimmer moves a repeating mask from position 200% to 0%, exactly one tile of width 2w for box width w, so it loops seamlessly: alpha(x) = g(((x / w - 2e) mod 2) / 2), with e the eased progress through each second and g(u) 1 for u <= 0.3, falling linearly to 0.65 at u = 0.8 and 0.65 to u = 1. The timing curve is CSS's default ease (cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)) applied per iteration.
With a delay nothing renders (and no space is taken) until 300ms (short), 1000ms (long) or the given ms pass; unmounting first cancels it.

semantics: The box exposes nothing to assistive technology: no role, label or busy state. The surrounding region should carry aria-busy or a status message while loading.

notes.text: The shimmer is a CSS mask animation gated on prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference; a native build reads the platform's reduce-motion setting, and when it animates must keep requesting frames while any skeleton is visible.

Under forced colours the box gains a 1px transparent outline inset 1px, which the system paints in its forced colour so the placeholder stays visible after its fill is removed. Native: in a forced-colour mode, stroke the box 1px in the system text colour.
--skeletonLoader-bgColor is a translucent neutral, so the box tints whatever surface it sits on rather than painting an opaque grey.
The 1rem default height, the gradient stops and the 200% mask size are literals; only the duration is a token, and the curve is CSS's default rather than a motion token.
